description:
About the Position

This FNS PhD examines secure management of 6G services distributed across infrastructure owned by different organisations. Its central problem is making dependable orchestration decisions across trust boundaries. TU Delft invites applications for a PhD position in this area: Secure Multi-stakeholder 6G Orchestration at TU Delft, Netherlands. The work sits within Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering. The host institution is in Delft, Netherlands. Full funding is provided; financial support is listed as €3,204/month. Applications close 1 November 2026.

Research Position Overview

Investigate attestation, trusted hardware, workload placement and auditable decisions. Extend open-source orchestration tools and evaluate them on experimental FNS infrastructure. TU Delft is seeking candidates for this PhD opportunity focused on Secure Multi-stakeholder 6G Orchestration at TU Delft, Netherlands. The work sits within Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering. The role is based in Delft, Netherlands. Funding covers the full cost of participation; financial support is listed as €3,204/month. The stated deadline is 1 November 2026.

Research Areas

  • 6G security
  • Trusted edge/cloud orchestration
  • Attestation and workload isolation

Use the application button on the official advert; email enquiries do not replace an online application.

About TU Delft and the Host Faculty

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, Netherlands. This position is hosted by the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Doctoral employment includes Graduate School training and supervision.
